tone_statements.citation: Pohlig, James N. 1992. Preliminary statement of phonemes in Besleri. Yaounde: SIL Cameroon, March 1992. 13 pp. (SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 47377; subject language Mina [hna]; 'Phonological Description').
tone_statements.quote: 4.0 Observations on Tone We note minimal tonal pairs as follows: [...] We see every suggestion in our data of a tonal system of two level tones, HIGH and LOW. A falling tone glide occurs habitually utterance-final from a HIGH tone: e.g., [nvâ] 'faeces' [hidîy] 'persons' [məfɛ̂s] 'little' which so far we would interpret as /nvá/, /hidíy/, and /məfɛ́s/. We find no evidence thus far of any tone glides word-internally.
tone_statements.locator: p. 11, section 4.0 'Observations on Tone' (also p. 1, NB under 1.1.1: 'we assume a tonal system of HIGH and LOW tones; we mark HIGH with [´] and leave LOW tone unmarked')
tone_statements.n_tones: 2 (H, L); utterance-final falling glide = allotone of H

sources.citation: Abdoulaye, Mahamane L. 2007. Review of Frajzyngier, Johnston & Edwards (2005), A Grammar of Mina. LINGUIST List 18.912 (27 March 2007; issue editor Laura Buszard-Welcher).
sources.note: Summarises Ch. 2: 28 consonant phonemes, six vowels /i, e, ə, u, o, a/, two vowel-harmony processes, phrase-internal final-vowel deletion (p. 21), syllable types V, N, VC, CV, CVC, CCV (p. 24); 'Mina has two tones, a High and a Low, which are associated with lexical and grammatical functions. The book claims that when a supporting vowel is deleted, the associated tone is deleted as well (p.29). Many grammatical markers display tonal polarity.' Nothing at all about stress or accent.
Nothing on phonology; names dialects Marbak, Kefedjevreng, Dzundzun (from the grammar p. 3) and cites only the grammar.

sources.citation: Gravina, Richard. 2014. The Phonology of Proto-Central Chadic: The reconstruction of the phonology and lexicon of Proto-Central Chadic, and the linguistic history of the Central Chadic languages. (LOT Dissertation Series 375.) Utrecht: LOT. 437 pp. PhD, Leiden.
sources.note: Comparative work; its only Mina source is Frajzyngier, Johnston & Edwards 2005. On Mina it says (p. 104) that there is no labialization prosody and the palatalization prosody only affects underlying /a/. Explicitly excludes stress: 'a reconstruction of the sound system of Proto-Central Chadic (though not including tone or stress)' and 'No attempt has been made to reconstruct tone or stress.' Nothing on Mina word stress.

sources.note: Two-day preliminary phonemic statement (6 short + 3 long vowels, consonant chart, syllable types V/CV/CVC) with sec. 4.0 'Observations on Tone' (p. 11): minimal tonal pairs ('make enter' vs 'marry', 'after, well then' vs 'wind'); a tonal system of two level tones, HIGH and LOW; a falling glide occurs utterance-finally on a HIGH tone (e.g. [nvâ] 'faeces', interpreted /nvá/); no tone glides word-internally. p. 1 NB: HIGH marked with acute, LOW unmarked throughout.
